Deadlock: a field guide for new players

Not sure what you just downloaded or what the hype is about? This guide covers what the game is, who to play, which mode to start in, and how to find your footing in this game.

The point is not to be an exhaustive summary of all there is to learn, but to get you from a state of confusion to a spot where you can learn the game in depth on your own terms, before you get to the point of frustration where you quit, feeling like you don’t even “get it”.

New here? Try the in-game tutorials first. They’re a little outdated and Valve will have to update them, but they still teach basics worth learning. This game is still in active development, by the way! You can give feedback on the Official Forums (get your login info in-game)!

What is Deadlock, actually?

Think of Deadlock as a MOBA first and a shooter second. You aim and shoot like in a third-person shooter, but the match is won the way a MOBA is won: by taking apart the enemy base.

The goal is to destroy the enemy Patron (the Ancient, Throne or Nexus of other games). You get there by taking down defenses in order:

Guardians›Walkers›Base Guardians›Shrines›Patron (2 Phases)
Kills are not the objective. A kill is a means to an end: it buys your team the time and space to take an objective, advance towards the enemy base or kill the Mid-Boss (Roshan/Nashor). This means your K/D/A matters much less than in hero shooters. A player with a 2–7 scoreline who farmed well and pushed lanes can be worth more than a 10–2 player who never touched an objective.

Deadlock expands the hero-shooter formula from a single objective to a large map with three lanes, a jungle full of opportunities and secondary objectives to manage a comeback!

Which mode should I play?

It depends on how quickly you want to jump in.

ModeWhat it isGood for
StandardThe real Deadlock.Jumping into the deep end. Fun right away if you can roll with the punches, overwhelming otherwise. So maybe try the following first.
Street BrawlThe quick, low-stakes casual mode. 4v4 in a single lane, round-based, no farming, about 15 minutes per match. Roguelike random item choices.Learning a character’s abilities and movement, and getting familiar with the laning terrain. It does not teach the rest of the main game.
Coop Bot matchA standard match against bots, with other players on your side who are usually happy to help.Getting to know the game without performance pressure or anxiety.
Explore NYCJust you and the map. There’s only the one.Getting your bearings before getting lost in the Cursed Apple. The map is big and has lots to see and do! More below.
RankedThe competitive mode.Taking things seriously. LOCK IN! (Locked until you are no longer new.)

Mode names and menus change between updates, so if something looks different in your client, check the in-game mode list.

Which character should I pick?

I love DPS characters in hero shooters or right-click MOBA carries I like supports, heals, and fights decided by ultimates. You said it’s a shooter second, right? I just want to brawl, I’ll worry about the nerd stuff later. I may be new but I’m moving different, gimme a chance
Pick anyone who looks cool. Then try them out in the Hideout or the Sandbox, and mess around in a bot game to see whether their playstyle clicks with you. Everything below is a starting point, not a rule.
NO ONE-TRICKS! Deadlock requires that you pick at least three characters you are willing to play before entering the queue, so do not tunnel-vision on a single character!

If you want an easier first pick, these are sorted by what you’re likely to enjoy already.

“I love DPS characters in hero shooters or right-click MOBA carries”

Strong gun damage plus abilities that are simple to use and fun to master. If you like winning fights by out-aiming people and ulting for aura, start here.

Shooting tip: while sliding, you do not consume ammo! Free bullets via rule of cool!

“I like supports, heals, and fights decided by ultimates. You said it’s a shooter second, right?”

Heals, shields, pushing power or an ultimate that swings a teamfight. You help your team win rather than winning alone.

“I just want to brawl, I’ll worry about the nerd stuff later.”

Get close, take hits, and swing. Big health pools and tools for team-fight mayhem make these a good fit for unga-bunga playstyles.

“I may be new but I’m moving different, gimme a chance”

If you have lots of experience in competitive hero shooters and love high-mobility characters, these will offer a satisfying challenge to learn.

We will cover the universal movement tech in its own chapter. I miss Titanfall and GunZ: The Duel….

Deep dive on the Deadlock Wiki: Heroes

“I was excited to play this hero-shooter but I just saw the item shop, I think I’m out!”

Don’t let the Curiosity Shop scare you! It’s true that you have to spend souls (your in-match money) on items that boost your health, damage and enhance your abilities.

But Deadlock has streamlined this MOBA-hurdle considerably and new players do NOT need to memorize every item or a meta-build.

Instead, you can use the most popular items section in the shop; it’s character-specific and based on recent data, so no wrong answers here for someone just learning the game.

You can also queue up community builds made by experienced players and automate the purchase of items in the correct order!

Press B (default key) to open the Shop Menu, click on “Build Browser” in the top right and then check “Public Builds” in the pop-up window.

In the settings, you can make the game automatically queue up your favorite build and it will buy the next item whenever you walk by a shop (the green shop icon ) or return to base.

Shop tips
  • There is a shop right next to the first Guardian in your lane, for as long as you can keep that Guardian standing. Once it falls, that shop closes for good.
  • Two shops are permanent: between the middle of the map and the outer lanes. Both teams can use them, so watch your back!
  • Or zipline back to base if there are no other safe options.
  • Pick a build for your characters before you even queue up, so you can focus on playing once the match starts!

We will cover what else you can find on the map in a later chapter.

Laning 101

We call the first part of a match the laning phase. You and a partner share a lane with two enemy players. Your instinct will say “fight players only, I can farm when they’re dead.” Resist it. This phase is about out-farming them, not brawling.

Use cover and move around to find better angles on troopers and players. Shoot players whenever there is no trooper or soul orb to worry about.

Last hits and denies

However, “last-hitting” works differently here than in most MOBAs. Because there isn’t any “last-hitting”, strictly speaking!

  • Troopers drop half of their soul value on the ground, no matter how they die.
  • The other half is released in a floating orb.
  • As long as you are close enough, you claim both automatically.

In Deadlock, it does not matter how enemy troopers die: you’ll get their full value just for being close by! But enemies complicate your “farming” as follows.

  • Floating orbs can be shot by either team. Shooting your own green orb is confirming it. Shooting the orange floating orbs denies its value to the enemy. You get it, instead.
  • Melee kills confirm the entire trooper’s value instantly. No orb for the enemy to deny.
  • Heavy melee is great in lane, but you can be parried. A new player is very likely to punch you back. So parry them!

For a deeper dive, the Deadlock Wiki strategy page covers matchups, wave priority and freezing a lane, and the soul orbs page has the details on orbs.

Sustain in lane

“I got low and now I can’t compete for souls!! How do I B?”

If you are a shot away from death, jump towards the zipline to heal in base. But this should be your last resort if you were caught out of position and barely survived.

If you’re not trading hits well, buy “Extra Regen”, “Healing Rite” or “Grit” for a shield.

There is also free healing marching down the lane. Banner-bearing troopers (also called Medic Troopers) are walking first aid kits: killing them and collecting their med-packs will heal you. They expire after 20 seconds, so with smart positioning, you will keep a health advantage over your opponents while denying them access!

Tip: Stick to cover from which you can still hit the troopers. On the sides of the lanes there are “Veils” (Cosmic Veils) to hide in, like League’s bushes or the treeline in Dota. Perfect for flanking players or hitting floating orbs safely!

Why farming wins

“I was winning fights but then we got steamrolled. Did the others feed?”

Souls make you level up, unlock abilities and buy items that raise your stats. When one character has more health, damage and tools than their opponent, the fight is likely decided before it starts.

This is not a hero shooter, so in the late game, you might feel like an opponent is unkillable… because they are, if you are on your own.
But that gap was created by dozens of decisions throughout the match, on both sides. You may have killed them twice in lane, but if they’re thousands of souls ahead ten minutes later, they ate their veggies while you rested on your laurels.

The good news: there are ways to come back!

But how can you tell how the game is going? Mostly, it is a combination of team net worth and map control, meaning who took more objectives and where the trooper waves are right now!

  • The top of your screen shows each player’s soul net worth and the team totals.
  • The eye symbol under the character images indicates whether their ultimate is ready. It unlocks at 3.8K, and if you get there first, you can likely go on the offensive in lane!
  • Kills only matter if you do something with the space and time won, like taking an objective.

But you may be wondering where else to get souls when you got bullied out of lane…

The map and the jungle

Jungling

“Jungling” refers to clearing neutral camps of NPCs known as “haunts” for souls. Deadlock has no dedicated jungler role thus far. Everyone can do it, though some characters clear faster than others. The jungle is a resource.

  • However, clearing a trooper wave is usually faster and pays more than a camp, so farm camps in between waves.
  • A camp’s respawn timer only starts once all its neutrals are dead, so clear the whole camp.
  • Watch out for roaming enemy players who like to steal souls you haven’t banked yet.

“What do you mean by smash and go?”

Boxes often contain free souls, and Golden Paper Stands (also called Buff Containers) often give you permanent buffs! So while you are going from place to place, smash those up!

“Did I just waste time on a virtual slot machine?”

Sort of! These machines show up from around the 8 minute mark. Heavy-punch it 4 times, then time your 5th heavy punch according to the lights at the top filling back up. Hit it right and you get souls and permanent buffs! Just know that it hits back every time you punch it, so keep your health up.

Universal movement tech

“I saw some shmovement in a clip. I just want a taste.”

As a new player, you probably only need the basics of stamina, dash-jumping, sliding and maybe wall-jumping. Here’s each one in brief.

  • Stamina. The bars under your crosshair. Air jumps, dashes and air dashes all spend them, and they refill over time. Most movement tech is really just spending stamina wisely.
  • Dash-jump. A fast long jump. Start a dash, then press jump the moment the stamina bar under your crosshair turns blue. It costs one extra stamina on top of the dash. Becoming consistent at this timing will win you every chase and escape against other new players.
  • Slide. Press crouch while you have enough speed (or while going down stairs and slopes) to slide. While sliding, you do not consume ammo! Free bullets via rule of cool!
  • Mantle glide. Crouch after mantling up for a speed boost: hold crouch while you climb a ledge and you’ll slide as soon as you get up.
  • Wall jump. Press jump next to a wall. The first one is free, and chaining more costs stamina and gets lower each time.
Doing these consistently will put you above most new players. Practice them in the Hideout or Sandbox. If you want a glimpse at the deep magics, check the wiki’s movement page and YouTube.

“I tried my best but some people got REALLY mad at me”

We’re generally a welcoming community, but some people take competitive games too seriously, even in unranked play. The good news: Deadlock has a Behavior System, so reports actually matter.

  • During a match, press Escape, click on their name and report them for harassment, griefing and similar.
  • You can mute them there as well.
  • You can also report after the game, on the scoreboard.

If your report is valid, the system might mute bad actors immediately, and could put them on time-out after the match or into Low Priority Queue, our jail for jerks.

Go and have some fun!

This is where we should take a break: go and play a few matches! Deadlock may have a lot to learn, but it can be enjoyed at all levels of play!

Item categories

“I played MOBAs and BRs, I get there’s items but what’s with these colours?”

Items are what’s making you stronger as the match goes on. Both gun damage and spirit (ability) damage grow over the course of a match, because you keep buying items that raise them. Characters also level up when they get souls (as a “BOON from your Patron”), so a fed enemy stacks both. This is why the farming advice matters so much.

The three item categories

Items come in three categories. You’ll see these colours in the shop, in your build and on the item tabs.

  • Weapon (orange) Boosts your gun damage and, depending on the item, also fire rate, ammo, reload and bullet effects. Also affects melee damage and SOME abilities!
  • Spirit (purple) Boosts your abilities’ damage and, depending on the item, cooldowns, range, duration and ability effects. Some abilities SCALE more with Spirit Power.
  • Vitality (green) Keeps you alive: health, regeneration, resistances, shields, healing and movement.

This means you can tell what kind of character and build you are picking based on colours alone! Mostly orange builds focus on your gun, mostly purple builds focus on your abilities! So if you picked a character because you wanted to point and shoot but the build is mostly purple, you are likely on a build that does not suit your expectations.

“My gun is a pea-shooter, theirs rips me to shreds.
My abilities tickle, theirs NUKE my health bar.
WTF?”

Not every character scales the same way

Different characters’ abilities scale with different stats. For many abilities, the bonus comes from spirit power. Others lean on your weapon, or on stats like health. Check an ability’s tooltip in the character screen, and look at the recommended builds for your character: they show what the community has found pays off, which is why “just follow a build” is a decent first plan.

Items can also do more than raise a number.

Some add new effects to your gunshots, such as slowing or poisoning enemies that you shoot.

Others change how your abilities behave, for example by adding lifesteal or a slow to one of them.

Others give you buttons to press, like a shield or a dash.

And some change what happens when you get hit, reducing incoming damage rather than adding anything to your attack.

Some items can be upgraded into stronger ones later, saving you inventory space, but you can sell an item back for part of its price in a pinch.

Inventory Space Tip: you start with a limited number of slots. Destroying enemy Walkers unlocks extra ones, which is another reason objectives matter.

Countering characters and effects

“That character seems OP, I had no chance from the beginning.”

They do not let me DO anything! What are these disables?!? Why is their gun SO much better, I am getting SHREDDED! I just got BLOWN UP by some particle effects I cannot even HIT them, man! They get to disengage for free or what? They are unkillable and take no damage! Raid-Boss TTK! I die instantly, no matter who I’m up against. So un-interactive and un-fun...

So you played a few matches and you already met a handful of characters you hate. Welcome to the community!

Sooner or later, you will encounter the equivalent of an MMO raid boss in your competitive multiplayer shooter. Before you rage about balance and uninstall, identify the problem: did you get stuck and could not move, could you not hit them, did their damage melt you, or did they not die? Each one has an answer in the shop. A character’s name is only the start, because the same character can beat you in different ways.

Don’t buy every counter. Buy the smallest useful answer, keep the core items that let you contribute, and ask your team who already has utility. Several of these are active items, so you press a button at the right moment instead of passively gaining stats. For a full list of items, see the wiki’s items page. The faces below are good examples of each problem.

“They do not let me DO anything! What are these disables?!?” (crowd control)

Stuns, slows and silences keep you from playing. Prevention, cleansing and surviving are separate jobs, and no single item covers all of them. Dispel Magic cleanses effects, Unstoppable lets you shrug off control for a short time, Indomitable automatically cleanses the next hard disable and rewards you with a barrier and shorter cooldowns, Reactive Barrier gives you a barrier whenever you get locked down, and Debuff Reducer shortens what lands on you.

“Why is their gun SO much better, I am getting SHREDDED!” (gun damage)

If a weapon character kills you before you can react, buy something for gun damage. Metal Skin is an active that gives you a short window to survive weapon damage and reach cover. Plated Armor gives lasting protection and Disarming Hex can shut their gun down. Weapon Shielding pops a barrier when a burst of weapon damage hits you, and Bullet Resilience adds bullet resist that grows once you’re low on health. Use cover too, because items won’t save you from standing in the open.

“I just got BLOWN UP by some particle effects” (spirit damage)

Many characters can build into Spirit Damage, but these are some of the usual suspects. Avoid their AoEs if possible, but some attacks will track you as well, and these defensive items will be your only saving grace if the enemy already got the souls to beef up their nukes. Spirit Shielding pops a barrier when a burst of spirit damage hits you, Spirit Resilience adds spirit resist that grows once you’re low on health, and Spellbreaker massively reduces the next big spirit hit you take.

“I cannot even HIT them, man! They get to disengage for free or what?” (mobility)

Fast, slippery characters need to be caught before you commit damage. Slowing Hex slows a target and can disable movement abilities. Knockdown is a delayed stun that grounds flying characters and interrupts channels, so have a follow-up ready. And Ethereal Shift lets you phase out of danger yourself.

“They are unkillable and take no damage! Raid-Boss TTK!” (healing and sustain)

If an enemy heals back everything your team deals, anti-heal is the answer. Healbane and Toxic Bullets reduce healing, and Decay is a spirit option. Pick the one you can apply reliably, then focus damage while the healing is cut.

Counters aren’t guarantees. Enemies may cleanse, dodge or shrug off your effect, so check the matchup and adapt.

Deep dive on the Deadlock Wiki: Items · Crowd Control

“I die instantly, no matter who I’m up against. So un-interactive and un-fun...”

Sounds like you either gotta beef up your resistances or get yourself a shield. Barriers soak up a burst of damage, and resistances make every hit count for less.

  • Weapon Shielding and Spirit Shielding automatically give you a barrier when you take a big burst of weapon or spirit damage in a short time.
  • Reactive Barrier gives you a barrier when you get stunned, chained, immobilized, slept or silenced, so a lockdown doesn’t mean a free kill.
  • Bullet Resilience and Spirit Resilience give you resistance to bullets or spirit damage, and extra of it once you’re below half health.
Early tip: an early item like Grit is great because it allows you to upgrade into an automatic response to bursts of damage or disables, depending on your needs. Weapon Shielding and Spirit Shielding answer damage, Reactive Barrier answers disables. In the first couple minutes, Extra Regen and Healing Rite can make a hard lane easier! And so do Healing Snacks!

Death Summary

“HOW DID I DIE THO?!? What even was that?”

When (not if) you die, you can click on your character-icon to the right-hand side of your screen to check which character damaged you in what way and what dealt the killing blow. The colours will also let you know what type of damage you are taking the most. That way you know what type of resistances you should buy next!

Deep dive on the Deadlock Wiki: Damage Barrier · Grit · Items

“Nah, the only good defense is a good offense. How do I take down THAT GUY on the other team?”

This opponent could be any character, really. But they are having a GOOD game and they made you feel it, too.

Team-coordination goes a long way, but if you want to wipe that smile off their face, consider the following options. Pricey, but potentially a total shut-down of their strongest asset.

Comebacks

“Why am I stuck in a 40 minute match when the game was over at 10 minutes, dude?”

The game is not over until the Patron is dead. If the enemy isn’t currently in your base or taking another objective worth defending, there are things you can do to come back! So if you see the net worth difference between the teams widening, consider the following options!

ObjectiveWhat it isWhenWhat it gives
Soul UrnA capture-the-flag type objective, asking you to take an Urn across the map.From 10:00, then every 5 minutesThe character who delivers it gets permanent buffs, plus a large amount of souls. Running it means carrying it while your team covers you.
Unstable RiftA king-of-the-hill type objective: stand in the capture zone on a side lane’s bridge.First between 10:00 and 12:00, then roughly every 6–8 minutesSouls for the winning team and a wave of Rift troopers. It expires if nobody wins it.
Mid-BossA tough neutral boss in the middle of the map.Appears early, but you will likely do it in the midgame when the enemy is deadThe Rejuvenator: team-wide buffs and instant respawns, ideal for a push, risky fights and ending the game in your favor.
Bridge BuffsA temporary buff you can pick up on the map.Every 5 minutesA massive boost for the next couple of minutes. It might put you on even footing with a higher net-worth foe.

Playing at a disadvantage

  • “Stop feeding” sounds like unhelpful advice, but what people are trying to tell you is to stop throwing yourself at the enemy when they’re ahead and you cannot outfight them.
  • Keep farming safely. Troopers and jungle camps still pay out when you’re behind.
  • Fight over Unstable Rifts. They give you defensive bonuses for being behind and a larger reward if you win. This is the #1 comeback mechanic in the game!
  • Counter-buy. Pick items that answer what’s beating you, such as bullet resistance against a heavy shooter.
  • Punish pushes. Objectives pull a team away from their base, which leaves undefended Guardians and Walkers.

Deep dive on the Deadlock Wiki: Soul Urn · Unstable Rift · Mid-Boss · Rejuvenator

The map

There is just the one map, so it’s worth walking around in the “Explore NYC” mode before your first real match. The basics:

  • Three lanes run from your base to theirs. Each has Guardians and a Walker, and troopers march down them. But without the players, this ritual would be stuck in a deadlock.
  • The Mid-Boss sits in the middle of the map. Killing it spawns the Rejuvenator, which gives your team strong buffs and quick respawns.
  • The jungle fills the space in between, with neutral camps, crates and shortcuts.
  • Defeating the Mid-Boss rewards the “Rejuvenator”. Provides a buff that gives your team three chances to revive on the spot if killed within the next few minutes.

Match schedule: there’s always something happening in the Cursed Apple

Keeping track of all the events happening throughout a match is beyond even intermediate players. But by being aware of the big ones coming up, you can be in the right position beforehand. Camps and some objectives start their respawn timer once you clear them, so don’t wait at an empty spot.

TimeEventWhen to go for it
0:00Trooper waves, every 30s (every 25s after 20:00, every 20s after 35:00)Always. Waves are your main income early, so don’t leave them for camps.
0:00Mid-Boss is available from the start. Respawns 7:00 after the first kill, 6:00 after the second, then 5:00.Not in the laning phase. Go for it in the midgame when the enemy is dead or pushed out. The Rejuvenator buff is great for ending the game.
2:00Small jungle camps, back 1:25 after a full clearBetween waves, to speed up your early farm.
3:00Crates and breakables, back 3:00 after breaking (some groups start at 5:00 or 10:00)On your way past. Cheap souls, no need to detour.
5:00Medium camps, back 4:50 after a full clearWhen your lane is stable and the next wave is not yet due.
5:00, then every 5:00Bridge buffs (a short stat boost)Grab it when it’s close to your fight or rotation. It’s a big edge if you’re behind.
6:00Zipline boost unlocksUse it to rotate, and take jump pads and teleporters when they’re faster.
8:00Large camps, back 5:35 after a full clear, and Sinner’s Sacrifice, back about 5:00 after a clearBig payouts but guarded. Go once you have the damage to clear them without dying.
10:00, then every 5:00Soul Urn, alternating lanes. The next one waits while an urn is being carried.When your team can cover the carrier. It’s a strong comeback pick if you’re behind.
10:00–12:00First Unstable Rift on a random side lane’s bridge, then roughly every 6–8 minutes. A visual effect shows up on the bridge about 80 seconds early, and an announcement comes 20 seconds before it opens.Fight for it, especially when behind. This is the best comeback mechanic in the game.
